transcript:
alex: quick proposal — add a per-request "precision negotiation" hint so clients can say quality vs cost, and server picks FP8/INT8/4-bit/FP16 path based on model, load, and recent regressions.
sasha: this came up in the RFC followup. what's the API shape you have in mind? is this just a hint or will we honor strictly?
alex: hint only. API example:
POST /v1/generate
{ "model": "redwood-1", "prompt": "...", "precision_hint": "balanced", "fallback_policy": "graceful" }
precision_hint choices: high_quality | balanced | low_cost
fallback_policy: strict | graceful | degrade-to-embedding
priya: important: we need clear eval gates. balanced -> should map to INT8 mostly, but only if eval on the prompt set shows <1% BLEU drop for that workload.
diego: runtime impact question — selecting per-request path might add decision latency. can we cache mapping by model+hint+region? also need to avoid hot locks when switching kernels.
matt: telemetry we need: (1) chosen_precision, (2) decision_reason (load|policy|regression), (3) quality_metric_delta, (4) rollback_flag. we should record these at token-level aggregation.
perf-bot: scheduled job added: perf/regressions/weekly for precision-path heatmap. Next run: 2026-03-21T04:00Z.
alex: good calls. propose decision flow:
1) client sends hint
2) server consults model-profile + live load SLOs + recent quality guardrails
3) pick candidate precision profile
4) if candidate flagged for recent regression -> if fallback_policy==strict return 503; if graceful try next candidate and mark shadow test
5) instrument and return chosen path
sasha: interface boundary: keep this entirely at the inference proxy layer (no model changes). model-serving only needs to expose supported precision variants and a perf/quality profile. keeps rollout safer.
priya: we also need a long-term refactor: centralize quantization metadata as a small manifest per model-version with fields: supported_precisions, eval_matrix (per task), stable_since, rollback_signal_id.
diego: implementation detail: we should avoid doing heavy eval at decision time. use precomputed scorecards and a short-lived cache (TTL 5m) for decisions. also ensure KV-cache compatibility for FP16 vs 4-bit hotpath.
matt: can we offer a non-blocking endpoint for clients to request a "guaranteed-quality" lane with SLA? that's basically Dedicated behavior but useful for embedded PLG clients.
alex: yes, SLA/guaranteed-quality maps to 'high_quality' + tag that disables dynamic routing. that'll be a separate flag requiring capacity reservations.
sasha: rollout plan:
- RFC final: add manifest spec
- dev: proxy changes + telemetry (2w)
- canary: 1% traffic shadowing precision decisions (3w)
- gate: quality regression alarms + automatic rollback
priya: eval tooling: add prompt-sampling helper to generate adversarial examples for each quant profile. we should run these inside CI and on canary telemetry.
diego: +1. note: kernel-selection heuristics need a small refactor so runtime can switch at request boundary without tearing session state.
alex: ok I'll draft a follow-up doc with API proto, manifest schema, and rollout checklist. ping me if you want to be on the review. thanks all :thumbsup:
